item.title: Man convicted of murder, armed robbery, and auto theft for 2-day crime spree in 2023

item.title: FBI agent highlights growing trend of online child exploitation
item.description: A special agent says the FBI has seen a rise in online crimes targeting children, with the most common being "sextortion" where adults use fake profiles to trick minors into sending sexual photos or videos and then use them as blackmail. Parents are advised to monitor their children's online activity and have open discussions about the dangers.

item.title: IU defensive coordinator Bryant Haines wins Broyles Award
item.description: Indiana University Defensive Coordinator Bryant Haines won the 30th Annual Broyles Award for the top assistant coach in college football, after helping lead the Hoosiers to their first National Championship appearance.

item.title: Eli Lilly stockpiles $1.5 billion of weight-loss drug ahead of FDA decision
item.description: Eli Lilly has $1.5 billion worth of pre-launch inventory of its experimental oral weight-loss drug, orforglipron, ahead of an expected FDA decision in April.

item.title: $90K of cocaine seized in Wayne County traffic stop
item.description: Terro Johnson was arrested after deputies found 2.2 pounds of cocaine, worth $90,000, in his car during a traffic stop.

item.title: Petyon Manning Children’s Hospital benefits from $25M raised at gala over 18 years
item.description: Peyton Manning hosted the 18th and final Celebration of Caring Gala. It's raised approximately $25 million for the Peyton Manning Children's Hospital at Ascension St. Vincent over nearly two decades.

item.title: Community comes together to honor memory of Hailey Buzbee
item.description: A celebration of life was held at ITOWN Church in Fishers, Indiana, for Hailey Buzbee, a Hamilton Southeastern High School student who was reported missing on Jan. 5, 2026, and later was found dead in Perry County, Ohio. Many people are the memorial wore her favorite color, pink.

item.title: IU educator arrested after Florida child solicitation sting operation
item.description: James K. Self, an Indiana University economics department director, was arrested in Bloomington on a preliminary charge of child solicitation following an undercover sting operation in Florida. After his arrest and jailing, Self was suspended from his job and banned from IU property.
